# `md/require-frontmatter-fields`

**A Markdown file's front matter carries the fields the project lists**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-data` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-data` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | Markdown |
| **Turned on by** | no preset — name it in `[rules]` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `fields` |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (the value of a field is the author's) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.2 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-unicorn/require-frontmatter-fields` |

## What it checks

A Markdown file starts with front matter that has every field in `fields`: `fields = ["title", "description"]` reports a file with no front matter, and one whose front matter has no `description`. A field counts when it is a key at the top of the block and has a value; `description:` with nothing after it, `""`, `[]`, `{}` and `null` are missing. YAML (`---`) and TOML (`+++`) front matter are both read; TOML only before its first table. The finding is one per file, on the front matter's first line (on the file's first line when there is none), and lists every field that is missing. An empty file is not reported. Behaviour of eslint-plugin-unicorn 79.0.0's `require-frontmatter-fields`, read and reimplemented.

With no `fields` set the rule is silent: it reports nothing, not even that the option is missing, and the engine does not run it on a single node. It is in no preset; a project switches it on under `[rules]` or in a `[scope.<name>]` for the folder whose pages need the fields (`files = ["docs/**/*.md"]`).

In `codelaw.toml`, under `[rules]`: `"md/require-frontmatter-fields" = { severity = "warn", options = { fields = ["title", "description"] } }`.

**Why:** A documentation site or a search index reads its page titles and summaries from front matter; a page without them shows up blank.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-data
pip install codelaw-rules-data
```

**No preset turns it on.** Load its pack through any preset (`codelaw:md/recommended` here), then name the rule in `[rules]`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:md/recommended"]

[rules]
"md/require-frontmatter-fields" = "error"
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"md/require-frontmatter-fields" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fields` | `string[]` | `[]` | the front matter fields every file needs, such as `title` and `description` |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."md/require-frontmatter-fields"]
severity = "error"

[rules."md/require-frontmatter-fields".options]
fields = []
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"md/require-frontmatter-fields" = { severity = "error", options = { fields = ["title"] } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `fields`

*string[]* · default `[]`

the front matter fields every file needs, such as `title` and `description`

```toml
[rules."md/require-frontmatter-fields".options]
fields = ["title"]
```

### Options in action

Each case below is one of the rule's tests (`packs/data/rules/md/require-frontmatter-fields.cases.md`): the options, the input, and what codelaw reports.

#### no front matter

```toml
[rules."md/require-frontmatter-fields".options]
fields = ["title"]
```

```md
# Setup
```

**Reports** at `1:1`.

#### a field is missing

```toml
[rules."md/require-frontmatter-fields".options]
fields = ["title", "description"]
```

```md
---
title: Setup
---

# Setup
```

**Reports** at `1:1`.

#### every field is there

```toml
[rules."md/require-frontmatter-fields".options]
fields = ["title", "description"]
```

```md
---
title: Setup
description: Install it
---

# Setup
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### a field with no value is missing

```toml
[rules."md/require-frontmatter-fields".options]
fields = ["title", "description"]
```

```md
---
title: Setup
description:
---

# Setup
```

**Reports** at `1:1`.

#### a list value counts

```toml
[rules."md/require-frontmatter-fields".options]
fields = ["tags"]
```

```md
---
tags:
  - a
---

# Setup
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### TOML front matter

```toml
[rules."md/require-frontmatter-fields".options]
fields = ["title", "description"]
```

```md
+++
title = "Setup"
+++

# Setup
```

**Reports** at `1:1`.

#### front matter that is not at the top is not front matter

```toml
[rules."md/require-frontmatter-fields".options]
fields = ["title"]
```

```md
# Setup

---
title: A
---
```

**Reports** at `1:1`.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — a scope of your own needs `files`:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.md"]
rules = { "md/require-frontmatter-fields" = { options = { fields = ["title"] } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.md"]
rules = { "md/require-frontmatter-fields" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"md/require-frontmatter-fields" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"md/require-frontmatter-fields" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"md/require-frontmatter-fields" = { severity = "warn", options = { fields = ["title"] } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "md/require-frontmatter-fields": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"fields": ["title"]}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **Markdown:** `<!-- codelaw-ignore md/require-frontmatter-fields: <reason> -->`
- **Dated:** `<!-- codelaw-ignore md/require-frontmatter-fields expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason> -->`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule md/require-frontmatter-fields --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain md/require-frontmatter-fields       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule md/require-frontmatter-fields  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>                 # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Add the missing fields to the file's front matter, or the front matter itself, with the values they need.
2. If the file is not one of the pages the fields are for, scope the rule away from it.

## Examples

### Markdown

#### Don't

*With these options:* `{ fields = ["title", "description"] }`

```md
---
title: Setup
---

# Setup
```

#### Do

*With these options:* `{ fields = ["title", "description"] }`

```md
---
title: Setup
description: Install and configure the tool
---

# Setup
```
